# UI RTL system

## When to use

Load this when the change touches layout, CSS, or components. The document direction is `rtl` for a Hebrew product. English fragments inside it stay LTR.

## Rules

1. Set the document once: `<html lang="he" dir="rtl">`. Do not sprinkle `dir` on every component. Override with `dir="ltr"` only for a LTR island.
2. Use CSS logical properties. Physical `left` / `right` and Tailwind `ml-*` `mr-*` `pl-*` `pr-*` `text-left` `text-right` are defects. Use `margin-inline`, `padding-inline`, `inset-inline-start`, `border-inline-start`, `text-align: start`.
3. Isolate bidirectional runs. Phones, emails, URLs, codes, and currency amounts go in `<bdi dir="ltr">` so Hebrew punctuation does not jump into them.
4. Use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` for columns of numbers.
5. Mirror icons that point along the reading direction (back, next, send, chevrons). Never mirror media controls, check marks, clocks, logos, or photographs. A volume slider is a physical scale, not a reading direction.
6. Copy `tokens.template.css` (installed to `.hebrew-skills/templates/tokens.template.css`, and beside this skill) to the app as `src/styles/tokens.css`. Keep the semantic names. Add a brand color there, not as a raw hex in a component.
7. Unpointed UI text uses about 1.6 line-height. Pointed text uses the nikud token (about 1.9). See `hebrew-content-nikud` before choosing a face for vowel marks. Heebo, Rubik, and Suez One are for unpointed UI and display, not for a nikud reading face.
8. Do not set `letter-spacing` above `0.02em` on Hebrew. Prefer `0`. If a Latin wordmark needs tracking, scope it with `:lang(en)`.
9. A physical property is allowed only for a third-party widget you cannot restyle, with `rtl-lint-disable-next-line` and a comment naming the widget.

## Examples

### Good

```html
<html lang="he" dir="rtl">
  <body>
    <p>התקשרו אל <bdi dir="ltr">03-555-0101</bdi></p>
  </body>
</html>
```

```css
.card {
  padding-inline: var(--space-4);
  border-inline-start: 3px solid var(--color-accent);
  text-align: start;
}
```

### Bad

```css
.card {
  padding-left: 16px;
  margin-right: 8px;
  text-align: right;
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;
}
```

`right` is not "the Hebrew side". It breaks the moment a LTR island or a translated screen appears.

## Checklist

- [ ] `html` has `lang="he"` and `dir="rtl"`.
- [ ] New CSS uses logical properties only.
- [ ] Phones, emails, URLs, and codes are in `bdi` with `dir="ltr"`.
- [ ] Directional icons are mirrored; media, checks, clocks, and logos are not.
- [ ] Colors and fonts come from the semantic tokens.
- [ ] Hebrew letter-spacing is 0, or under 0.02em with a reason.
